assumptions: A candidate's power is its power at the effect that matters, and its alpha the size it will be run at; the gain is no better than those two numbers.
The belief a test is ranked against is the ledger's elicited belief for that hypothesis, or one the caller supplied.
`measurements` assumes a normal quantity with known noise; `trials` assumes exchangeable draws at one rate.
limits: An informative test is not a test worth running: a high gain on a hypothesis nobody cares about is still high.
Two candidates reading the same data are not two independent looks; the overlap is named, never subtracted, because what it costs depends on how each test uses the data.
A hypothesis with no recorded belief is not ranked, since an invented prior would decide the order.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which candidate experiment would teach the most about the hypothesis it is registered against, and how much of it is worth running?

description: Rank candidate experiments by what running them would TEACH — Lindley's expected information gain, the drop in uncertainty about a hypothesis expected before anything is run. Three grains: `tests` ranks candidate falsification tests against the beliefs a discovery ledger holds, each with the posterior its two outcomes would leave, by gain and separately by gain per unit cost; `measurements` says what n readings of a normal quantity would teach, and how many it takes to reach a target; `trials` says the same for a rate held as a Beta. A gain is what a result would settle whichever way it lands — never evidence that a hypothesis is true, which stays with the ledger's e-values.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: the Beta prior's α — successes already believed in. Only applies when mode is trials.

beliefs.description: belief that each hypothesis is true, as `{hypothesisId: probability}` — given directly, or to override the ledger's. Only applies when mode is tests.

beta.description: the Beta prior's β — failures already believed in. Only applies when mode is trials.

ledger.description: a jane.discovery-ledger file, as `run_discovery_programme` returns: its elicited beliefs and the sources its evidence already read. Only applies when mode is tests.

mode.description: which grain of the question: rank candidate tests, size a run of measurements, or size a run of trials. Values: tests (Candidate tests), measurements (Measurements of a mean), trials (Trials of a rate).

n.description: how many measurements the run would take. Only applies when mode is measurements.

noise_sd.description: the measurement noise, in the same units. Only applies when mode is measurements.

prior_sd.description: how uncertain the mean is now, as a standard deviation. Only applies when mode is measurements.

target_bits.description: a gain to reach: the answer says how many measurements it would take. Only applies when mode is measurements.

tests.description: the candidates, each `{id, hypothesis, power, alpha}` and optionally `cost`, `reads` (what it would read) and `label`. Only applies when mode is tests.

trials.description: how many trials the run would take. Only applies when mode is trials.

name: rank_next_tests

beliefs.description: the belief each hypothesis was ranked against, and where it came from

best.description: the most informative candidate's id, or the mode's own answer in words

bits.description: the expected information gain of the top answer, in bits

byCost.description: the same candidates ordered by gain per unit cost, when every one was priced

gain.description: the gain itself: nats, bits, and the entropies before and after. Absent when candidate tests were ranked, where each one carries its own

note.description: why a ranking is short or empty, when it is

ranked.description: every ranked candidate: gain, gain per unit cost, the prior it stands on and the posterior each outcome would leave

result.description: the full answer, with the settings that produced it

samplesForTarget.description: how many measurements reach `target_bits`; null when no target was set
